source: NCERT Class X, India and the Contemporary World II, History Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. The First World War and Gandhi's Early Struggles
points: **World War I** brought high taxes, forced recruitment and price rises — spreading discontent.
**Gandhi** returned from South Africa (1915) with the method of **Satyagraha** (truth-force / non-violent resistance).
Early successes: **Champaran (1917, indigo), Kheda (1918, peasants), Ahmedabad (1918, mill workers)**.

sections.heading: 2. Rowlatt Act and Non-Cooperation
points: The **Rowlatt Act (1919)** allowed detention without trial → nationwide protest.
**Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919, Amritsar)** — General **Dyer** fired on an unarmed crowd, killing hundreds → outrage.
**Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22)** — boycott of schools, courts, titles, foreign cloth; combined with the **Khilafat** issue (Hindu-Muslim unity).
Called off after the violence at **Chauri Chaura (Feb 1922)**.

sections.heading: 3. Civil Disobedience Movement
points: **Purna Swaraj** (complete independence) declared at the **Lahore Congress (1929)**; **26 January 1930** = first Independence Day.
**Civil Disobedience Movement (1930)** began with the **Dandi Salt March** (Gandhi, 240 miles) — breaking the **salt law**.
People broke colonial laws, boycotted foreign goods; **Round Table Conferences** (London) followed.
The **Gandhi–Irwin Pact (1931)** and the **Poona Pact (1932)** (with Ambedkar, on separate electorates for Dalits) were key events.

sections.heading: 4. The Sense of Collective Belonging
points: Nationalism spread through **symbols and images**: **'Bharat Mata'** (painted by Abanindranath Tagore), folklore, a national **flag** (Swaraj flag with the charkha).
Songs — **'Vande Mataram'** (Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay).
Reinterpretation of **history** built pride; participation grew across classes, though with internal differences.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Satyagraha (Gandhi); early: Champaran 1917, Kheda & Ahmedabad 1918.
Rowlatt Act 1919 → Jallianwala Bagh (13 Apr 1919, Dyer, Amritsar).
Non-Cooperation 1920–22 (with Khilafat) ended after Chauri Chaura (1922).
Purna Swaraj at Lahore 1929; Civil Disobedience 1930 = Dandi Salt March.
Poona Pact 1932 (Gandhi-Ambedkar); Bharat Mata (Abanindranath Tagore); Vande Mataram (Bankim Chandra).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Non-Cooperation (1920–22)** ended after **Chauri Chaura**; **Civil Disobedience (1930)** began with the **Salt March**.
**Jallianwala Bagh = 1919** (General Dyer); **Rowlatt Act = 1919**.
**Bharat Mata** was painted by **Abanindranath Tagore**; **Vande Mataram** written by **Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay**.
The **Poona Pact (1932)** was between **Gandhi and Ambedkar** (on Dalit representation).
